1
Haye Sughra Da Shehanshah Veeran Ali Akbar V Ro Paya.
Phophiyaan De Naal Bhaina Jadoon Sughra Nu Seene La Ke Kita Si Alwida.
Akbar Ne Rondiyaan Ayho Sughra Nu Aakhiya.
Wada Aye Bhain Meri Tere Kool Aon Da.
Har Haal Che Main Aawan Ga Wada Aye Bhain Mera Jay Jonda Reh Gaya.
Chawaan Di Ja Nayi Othe Shagna Di Aas Nayi.
Mohlat Nayi Othe Honi Sano Sehray Lan Di.
Oss Shehar Ja Ray Aan Asi Jis Shehar Nu Zamana Kehnda Aye Karbala.
Safraan Da Koi Dukh Tainu Na Wekhna Paway.
Tere Toon Sham Da Har Sada Gham Paraan Raway.
Na Kofa Sham Wekhein Kadi Sughra Tere Layi Aye Akbar Di Aye Dua.
Sughra Ne Aakhiya Menu De Ja Ijazataan.
Jad Yaad Aaway Teri Tainu Main Pukar Laan.
Toon Janda Aein Jay Main Kawaan Awaz Tay Kare Gi Melaan Da Fasla.
Quran-e-Syeda Diyaan Aytaan Wichar Gayiyaan.
Qabraan V Ais Ghar Di Kitay Naal Na Raiyaan.
Do Noor Ho Gaye Ne Juda Akbar Juda Nayi Hoye Do Bhain Te Bhira.

from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
p = Path('src/data/lyrics/haye-sughra-da-shehanshah-veeran-ali-lyrics-2018-tajpoints-a66eaa16689caaff18ee.md')
s = p.read_text().replace('tere kol aon da','tere kool aon da').replace('اجازتـاں','اجازتاں')
p.write_text(s.rstrip('\\n')+'\\n')
before = subprocess.check_output(['git','show',f'HEAD:{p}'], text=True).split('---',2)[2].strip().splitlines()
header, body = s.split('---',2)[1:]
roman = header.split('romanLyrics: |-\\n')[1].strip().splitlines()
source = body.strip().splitlines()
assert [line.strip().casefold() for line in roman] == [line.rstrip('.').casefold() for line in before]
assert roman[0] == '1' and source[0] == '۱' and len(roman) == len(source) == 18
assert '\\u200c' not in s
print('Verified 17 matching verse positions and preserved Roman wording.')
PY

item.text:
Reconstructed all 17 verses in Shahmukhi and preserved the Roman wording in `romanLyrics`. Updated the language metadata to Punjabi because the verses consistently use Punjabi grammar, and removed the resolved `noUrdu` tag.

Both versions contain one 17-verse stanza in the same order. The Roman readings “Veeran” and “har sada” were rendered as `ویراں` and `ہر سدا`.
